Checking the policy against the results:

- Duplicates: T7 shows no hits, so no flag.
- Model: The label photo (T1) is legible and reads DT2E. That is not a recalled model (R:models lists DR2A and DR2E). The typed model matches the label reading (T2 mismatch). Per policy, a legible label showing a non-recalled model means deny. The typed model isn't a typo of a recalled model here; DT2E is a different model string from DR2E, and the label itself is the evidence.
- Serial, date code, purchase, and destruction checks all pass (T3, T4, T5, T6), but the model failure controls.

Outcome: deny.

reasons.text: The label photo is legible and shows model DT2E, which is not on the recalled model list (DR2A, DR2E). Under the claim policy, a legible label showing a non-recalled model means the unit is not part of this recall.
The typed model DT2E also does not match any recalled model, so the model check fails on both the label and the typed value.
No duplicate claims were found, so the denial does not rest on a duplicate flag.
Serial number, date code, retailer, and purchase window all pass, but these do not override the model failure.
